statement: Antibiotics are effective against colds and flu.
People with a common cold usually need antibiotics to recover.
Some infections caused by bacteria can get better without antibiotics.
It's okay to use antibiotics that were given to a friend or family member, as long as they were used to treat the same illness.
It's okay to buy the same antibiotics, or ask a doctor for them, if they helped you get better when you had the same symptoms before.
Taking antibiotics often has side effects such as diarrhoea.
In India, a vertical red line on a medicine strip means it should be taken only with a doctor's prescription.
If you are prescribed antibiotics and start to feel better, what should you do?
Rinsing hands with plain water for 2-3 seconds is enough to remove most germs.
Vaccines can reduce the need for antibiotics by preventing infections.
Bacteria which are resistant to antibiotics can be spread from person to person.
Antibiotic resistance occurs when your body becomes resistant to antibiotics and they no longer work as well.
Antibiotic resistance is only a problem for people who take antibiotics regularly.
Unnecessary use of antibiotics makes them become ineffective.
Antibiotic-resistant infections could make medical procedures like surgery and cancer treatment much more dangerous.
